title: Long-term proton pump inhibitors and risk of gastric cancer development after treatment for Helicobacter pylori: a population-based study
authors: Cheung KS, Chan EW, Wong AYS, Chen L, Wong ICK, Leung WK
population: Hong Kong adults who received clarithromycin-based triple therapy for Helicobacter pylori, 2003 to 2012, excluding treatment failure, gastric cancer within 12 months and gastric ulcer after therapy; PPI or H2-receptor antagonist prescriptions within 6 months before cancer excluded
funder: Not read: the publisher page refused access and the article is not in PubMed Central.
authorConflicts: WKL received honoraria for advisory board meetings of Takeda and Abbott Laboratories (abstract record).
result: 153 (0.24%) developed gastric cancer. PPI use HR 2.44 (95% CI 1.42 to 4.20); H2-receptor antagonists, a negative control exposure, HR 0.72 (0.48 to 1.07). HR 5.04 (1.23 to 20.61), 6.65 (1.62 to 27.26) and 8.34 (2.02 to 34.41) for at least 1, 2 and 3 years of use. Adjusted absolute risk difference 4.29 (1.25 to 9.54) excess gastric cancers per 10,000 person-years.
